title: One-Step Equations
note: Import with POST /api/admin/math-templates/import?subject=Solve-Easy-Equations . Every template's category is One-Step-Equations. Subject names are unique, so the existing Solve-Easy-Equations and One-Step-Equations folders are reused when they already exist.

templates.label: Solve x + a = b
templates.subject: Math
templates.explanation: Undo the addition: subtract a from both sides, so x = b − a.
templates.grading_requirements: Exact value; fractions (e.g. 7/3) and exact decimals are both accepted.

templates.label: Solve x − a = b
templates.subject: Math
templates.explanation: Undo the subtraction: add a to both sides, so x = b + a.
templates.grading_requirements: Exact value; fractions (e.g. 7/3) and exact decimals are both accepted.

templates.label: Solve a + x = b
templates.subject: Math
templates.explanation: Subtract a from both sides, so x = b − a.
templates.grading_requirements: Exact value; fractions (e.g. 7/3) and exact decimals are both accepted.

templates.label: Solve b = x + a (variable on the right)
templates.subject: Math
templates.explanation: Subtract a from both sides, so x = b − a.
templates.grading_requirements: Exact value; fractions (e.g. 7/3) and exact decimals are both accepted.

templates.label: Solve x + (−a) = b
templates.subject: Math
templates.explanation: Adding −a is the same as subtracting a. Add a to both sides, so x = b + a.
templates.grading_requirements: Exact value; fractions (e.g. 7/3) and exact decimals are both accepted.

templates.label: Solve x − (−a) = b
templates.subject: Math
templates.explanation: Subtracting −a is the same as adding a. Subtract a from both sides, so x = b − a.
templates.grading_requirements: Exact value; fractions (e.g. 7/3) and exact decimals are both accepted.

templates.label: Solve x + a = b with decimals
templates.subject: Math
templates.explanation: Subtract a from both sides and line up the decimal points: x = b − a.
templates.grading_requirements: Exact value; fractions (e.g. 7/3) and exact decimals are both accepted.

templates.label: Solve ax = b
templates.subject: Math
templates.explanation: Undo the multiplication: divide both sides by a, so x = b ÷ a.
templates.grading_requirements: Exact value; fractions (e.g. 7/3) and exact decimals are both accepted.

templates.label: Solve x/a = b
templates.subject: Math
templates.explanation: Undo the division: multiply both sides by a, so x = a · b.
templates.grading_requirements: Exact value; fractions (e.g. 7/3) and exact decimals are both accepted.

templates.label: Solve −x = b
templates.subject: Math
templates.explanation: −x means −1 · x. Divide (or multiply) both sides by −1, so x = −b.
templates.grading_requirements: Exact value; fractions (e.g. 7/3) and exact decimals are both accepted.

templates.label: Solve ax = b (fraction answer)
templates.subject: Math
templates.template: Solve for \(x\): \({a}x = {b}\) Write your answer as a fraction in simplest form or as a decimal.
templates.template_latex: Solve for \(x\): \({a}x = {b}\) Write your answer as a fraction in simplest form or as a decimal.
templates.explanation: Divide both sides by a. The quotient is not a whole number, so write x = b/a in lowest terms.
templates.grading_requirements: Exact value; fractions (e.g. 7/3) and exact decimals are both accepted.

example.question_latex: Solve for \(x\): \(8x = -17\) Write your answer as a fraction in simplest form or as a decimal.

templates.label: Solve ax = b with a decimal coefficient
templates.subject: Math
templates.explanation: Divide both sides by the decimal a, so x = b ÷ a.
templates.grading_requirements: Exact value; fractions (e.g. 7/3) and exact decimals are both accepted.

templates.label: Solve ax − b = c
templates.subject: Math
templates.explanation: First add b to both sides (ax = c + b), then divide by a: x = (c + b) ÷ a.
templates.grading_requirements: Exact value; fractions (e.g. 7/3) and exact decimals are both accepted.

templates.label: Solve ax + b = c
templates.subject: Math
templates.explanation: First subtract b from both sides (ax = c − b), then divide by a: x = (c − b) ÷ a.
templates.grading_requirements: Exact value; fractions (e.g. 7/3) and exact decimals are both accepted.

templates.label: Solve x/a + b = c
templates.subject: Math
templates.explanation: First subtract b from both sides (x/a = c − b), then multiply by a: x = a(c − b).
templates.grading_requirements: Exact value; fractions (e.g. 7/3) and exact decimals are both accepted.

templates.label: Solve x/a = b/c (whole-number answer)
templates.subject: Math
templates.explanation: Multiply both sides by a (or cross-multiply: c·x = a·b), so x = a·b ÷ c.
templates.grading_requirements: Exact value; fractions (e.g. 7/3) and exact decimals are both accepted.

templates.label: Solve x/a = b/c (fraction answer)
templates.subject: Math
templates.template: Solve for \(x\): \(\frac{x}{{a}} = \frac{{b}}{{c}}\) Write your answer as a fraction in simplest form or as a decimal.
templates.template_latex: Solve for \(x\): \(\frac{x}{{a}} = \frac{{b}}{{c}}\) Write your answer as a fraction in simplest form or as a decimal.
templates.explanation: Multiply both sides by a: x = a·b/c, then simplify the fraction.
templates.grading_requirements: Exact value; fractions (e.g. 7/3) and exact decimals are both accepted.

example.question_latex: Solve for \(x\): \(\frac{x}{4} = \frac{9}{11}\) Write your answer as a fraction in simplest form or as a decimal.

templates.label: Solve a/x = b/c
templates.subject: Math
templates.explanation: Cross-multiply: b·x = a·c, then divide by b, so x = a·c ÷ b.
templates.grading_requirements: Exact value; fractions (e.g. 7/3) and exact decimals are both accepted.

templates.label: Solve (a/b)x = c
templates.subject: Math
templates.explanation: Multiply both sides by the reciprocal b/a, so x = c · b/a.
templates.grading_requirements: Exact value; fractions (e.g. 7/3) and exact decimals are both accepted.

templates.label: Solve x + a/b = c/d
templates.subject: Math
templates.template: Solve for \(x\): \(x + \frac{{a}}{{b}} = \frac{{c}}{{d}}\) Write your answer as a fraction in simplest form or as a decimal.
templates.template_latex: Solve for \(x\): \(x + \frac{{a}}{{b}} = \frac{{c}}{{d}}\) Write your answer as a fraction in simplest form or as a decimal.
templates.explanation: Subtract a/b from both sides with a common denominator: x = c/d − a/b.
templates.grading_requirements: Exact value; fractions (e.g. 7/3) and exact decimals are both accepted.

example.question_latex: Solve for \(x\): \(x + \frac{1}{4} = \frac{9}{7}\) Write your answer as a fraction in simplest form or as a decimal.

templates.label: Word problem: age difference (x + a = b)
templates.subject: Math
templates.template: Tom is {a} years older than his sister Mia. Tom is {b} years old. Write an equation and solve it to find Mia's age.
templates.template_latex: Tom is {a} years older than his sister Mia. Tom is {b} years old. Write an equation and solve it to find Mia's age.
templates.explanation: Let x be Mia's age. Then x + a = b, so x = b − a.
templates.grading_requirements: Exact value; fractions (e.g. 7/3) and exact decimals are both accepted.

example.question_latex: Tom is 4 years older than his sister Mia. Tom is 20 years old. Write an equation and solve it to find Mia's age.

templates.label: Word problem: money spent (x − a = b)
templates.subject: Math
templates.template: After spending \(\${a}\) on a jacket, Ana has \(\${b}\) left. How many dollars did she have before buying the jacket?
templates.template_latex: After spending \(\${a}\) on a jacket, Ana has \(\${b}\) left. How many dollars did she have before buying the jacket?
templates.explanation: Let x be the starting amount. Then x − a = b, so x = b + a.
templates.grading_requirements: Exact value; fractions (e.g. 7/3) and exact decimals are both accepted.

example.question_latex: After spending \(\$23\) on a jacket, Ana has \(\$136\) left. How many dollars did she have before buying the jacket?

templates.label: Word problem: temperature drop (x − a = b)
templates.subject: Math
templates.template: The temperature dropped {a}\(^\circ\)F overnight. In the morning it was {b}\(^\circ\)F. What was the temperature the evening before, in \(^\circ\)F?
templates.template_latex: The temperature dropped {a}\(^\circ\)F overnight. In the morning it was {b}\(^\circ\)F. What was the temperature the evening before, in \(^\circ\)F?
templates.explanation: Let x be the evening temperature. Then x − a = b, so x = b + a.
templates.grading_requirements: Exact value; fractions (e.g. 7/3) and exact decimals are both accepted.

example.question_latex: The temperature dropped 5\(^\circ\)F overnight. In the morning it was 15\(^\circ\)F. What was the temperature the evening before, in \(^\circ\)F?

templates.label: Word problem: price of one item (ax = b)
templates.subject: Math
templates.template: {a} movie tickets cost \(\${b}\) in total. Each ticket costs the same. What is the price of one ticket, in dollars?
templates.template_latex: {a} movie tickets cost \(\${b}\) in total. Each ticket costs the same. What is the price of one ticket, in dollars?
templates.explanation: Let x be the price of one ticket. Then a·x = b, so x = b ÷ a.
templates.grading_requirements: Exact value; fractions (e.g. 7/3) and exact decimals are both accepted.

example.question_latex: 8 movie tickets cost \(\$48\) in total. Each ticket costs the same. What is the price of one ticket, in dollars?

templates.label: Word problem: splitting a bill (x/a = b)
templates.subject: Math
templates.template: {a} friends split a restaurant bill equally. Each friend pays \(\${b}\). What was the total bill, in dollars?
templates.template_latex: {a} friends split a restaurant bill equally. Each friend pays \(\${b}\). What was the total bill, in dollars?
templates.explanation: Let x be the total bill. Then x/a = b, so x = a · b.
templates.grading_requirements: Exact value; fractions (e.g. 7/3) and exact decimals are both accepted.

example.question_latex: 5 friends split a restaurant bill equally. Each friend pays \(\$11\). What was the total bill, in dollars?

templates.label: Word problem: rectangle length (wx = A)
templates.subject: Math
templates.template: A rectangle has an area of {A} square feet and a width of {w} feet. What is its length, in feet?
templates.template_latex: A rectangle has an area of {A} square feet and a width of {w} feet. What is its length, in feet?
templates.explanation: Area = length × width, so w·x = A and x = A ÷ w.
templates.grading_requirements: Exact value; fractions (e.g. 7/3) and exact decimals are both accepted.

example.question_latex: A rectangle has an area of 84 square feet and a width of 12 feet. What is its length, in feet?

templates.label: Word problem: constant speed (tx = d)
templates.subject: Math
templates.template: A car travels {d} miles in {t} hours at a constant speed. What is its speed, in miles per hour?
templates.template_latex: A car travels {d} miles in {t} hours at a constant speed. What is its speed, in miles per hour?
templates.explanation: Distance = speed × time, so t·x = d and x = d ÷ t.
templates.grading_requirements: Exact value; fractions (e.g. 7/3) and exact decimals are both accepted.

example.question_latex: A car travels 144 miles in 4 hours at a constant speed. What is its speed, in miles per hour?

templates.label: Word problem: recipe proportion (x/c = a/b)
templates.subject: Math
templates.template: A recipe uses {a} cups of flour to make {b} muffins. How many cups of flour are needed to make {c} muffins?
templates.template_latex: A recipe uses {a} cups of flour to make {b} muffins. How many cups of flour are needed to make {c} muffins?
templates.explanation: Set up the proportion x/c = a/b and multiply both sides by c: x = a·c ÷ b.
templates.grading_requirements: Exact value; fractions (e.g. 7/3) and exact decimals are both accepted.

example.question_latex: A recipe uses 2 cups of flour to make 8 muffins. How many cups of flour are needed to make 12 muffins?

templates.label: Word problem: map scale (ax = b)
templates.subject: Math
templates.template: On a map, 1 inch represents {a} miles. Two towns are {b} miles apart. How many inches apart are they on the map?
templates.template_latex: On a map, 1 inch represents {a} miles. Two towns are {b} miles apart. How many inches apart are they on the map?
templates.explanation: Let x be the map distance. Then a·x = b, so x = b ÷ a (a decimal such as 2.5 is fine).
templates.grading_requirements: Exact value; fractions (e.g. 7/3) and exact decimals are both accepted.

example.question_latex: On a map, 1 inch represents 8 miles. Two towns are 100 miles apart. How many inches apart are they on the map?

templates.label: Word problem: gym membership (ax + b = c)
templates.subject: Math
templates.template: A gym charges a \(\${b}\) sign-up fee plus \(\${a}\) per month. Jordan paid \(\${c}\) in total. For how many months did Jordan pay?
templates.template_latex: A gym charges a \(\${b}\) sign-up fee plus \(\${a}\) per month. Jordan paid \(\${c}\) in total. For how many months did Jordan pay?
templates.explanation: Let x be the number of months. Then a·x + b = c; subtract b, then divide by a.
templates.grading_requirements: Exact value; fractions (e.g. 7/3) and exact decimals are both accepted.

example.question_latex: A gym charges a \(\$26\) sign-up fee plus \(\$36\) per month. Jordan paid \(\$170\) in total. For how many months did Jordan pay?

templates.label: Word problem: taxi fare (ax + b = c)
templates.subject: Math
templates.template: A taxi charges \(\${b}\) to start plus \(\${a}\) per mile. A ride costs \(\${c}\). How many miles long was the ride?
templates.template_latex: A taxi charges \(\${b}\) to start plus \(\${a}\) per mile. A ride costs \(\${c}\). How many miles long was the ride?
templates.explanation: Let x be the miles. Then a·x + b = c; subtract b, then divide by a.
templates.grading_requirements: Exact value; fractions (e.g. 7/3) and exact decimals are both accepted.

example.question_latex: A taxi charges \(\$3\) to start plus \(\$2.75\) per mile. A ride costs \(\$36\). How many miles long was the ride?

templates.label: Word problem: shared candy (x/a = b)
templates.subject: Math
templates.template: A bag of candy is shared equally among {a} students, and each student gets {b} pieces. How many pieces were in the bag?
templates.template_latex: A bag of candy is shared equally among {a} students, and each student gets {b} pieces. How many pieces were in the bag?
templates.explanation: Let x be the number of pieces. Then x/a = b, so x = a · b.
templates.grading_requirements: Exact value; fractions (e.g. 7/3) and exact decimals are both accepted.

example.question_latex: A bag of candy is shared equally among 11 students, and each student gets 3 pieces. How many pieces were in the bag?
